messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High 5xx/error rate from private-gateway-uaenorth (dedicated egress). Trigger: frontend 502 spike > 15% for 3m :rotating_light:

sylvia chen: seeing this too, internal dashboards show RTT spike and 502s from sessions that route via the uaenorth egress. Lots of our Private customers reporting failures.

cheng li: oncall here, paging netinfra. @omar can you take BGP/net path? suspecting multipath route oscillation between Azure transit and partner on-prem link.

omar al-hassan: on it. grabbing flow logs now. can you share sample request ids or IPs?

sylvia chen: sample trace id: trace-uae-01 (attached in logs). customer requests NGINX->gw translated -> 10.4.2.1 egress IP. When 502s happen we see connection reset from backend and DNS NXDOMAIN on private-resolver for a subset of prefixes.

katie nguyen: customer-success getting tickets from 3 customers (Acct: ORCH, NOVA, RIV). CSU says failures started ~ 2024-11-07T02:35Z. We need impact matrix ASAP: % failing requests, degradations, and any auth failures.

cheng li: quick checks:
```
# check our egress gateways health
kubectl get pods -n redwood-egress -o wide | grep uaenorth
# check iptables conntrack/backlog
ssh gateway-uae-01 -- sudo conntrack -L | tail -n 50
```
I also kicked off `az network watcher packet-capture` against the gateway subnet to capture when the next failure hits.

raj patel: I pulled system logs: seeing repeated TCP RSTs toward one upstream provider ASN and DNS responses alternating between our custom resolver and Azure-provided resolver. Looks like path-bouncing may be causing intermittent upstream TCP handshake failures.

omar al-hassan: Azure confirmed they're seeing flapping on peering with PartnerX in uaenorth. Support case 21098765 opened. Azure: "We observe active multipath route withdrawals and re-announcements due to control-plane instability on PartnerX side."

sylvia chen: action plan: 1) divert affected prefix to backup transit in region (backup-transit-uae) 2) enable short-term traffic-pinning on affected flows (sticky session) 3) enable local DNS fallback to resolv.conf backup for private subnets.

katie nguyen: notifying customers: sending short advisory that we're investigating and applying mitigations. CSU will ask for log traces and advise on retry/backoff.

cheng li: implementing diversion now. Command executed: `ip rule add from 10.4.2.0/24 table backup-transit-uae priority 200` then `ip route replace default via 10.8.1.1 table backup-transit-uae` — verifying BGP adverts.

incident-bot: Deploy event: route-diversion-uae started by cheng li at 1765432365. Postmortem tag: incident/uae-egress-multipath-1765432109.

omar al-hassan: after diversion we see backend success rate improve to ~97% from ~82%. Some sessions still hit older path due to sticky NAT state. Clearing conntrack entries on gateways reduced residual errors.

raj patel: note: DNS TTLs were low but cached resolvers on customer on-prem still returning stale records — we should advise customers to flush DNS caches. Also observed ephemeral increase in latency (p50 +40ms) during cutover.

sylvia chen: customer impact summary (preliminary):
- Affected customers: ORCH, NOVA, RIV (partial: ~20-40% of requests failing)
- Symptom: 502s and intermittent DNS NXDOMAIN for private resolver queries
- Window: 2024-11-07T02:35Z -> ongoing mitigation (diversion applied 02:56Z)
- Partial mitigation success: successful request rate improved to 95-98% after diversion and conntrack purge

katie nguyen: we've posted a status update to customers citing temporary routing issue with partner and that we've applied a regional diversion. CSU will follow up once Azure confirms fix.

cheng li: handoff to next oncall in 60m. next oncall: @oncall-shadow. Key tasks for handoff: monitor packet-capture for recurrence, keep Azure support case open, coordinate with PartnerX for a permanent peering fix, and validate route stability for 1h after handoff.

oncall-shadow: acknowledged. I will monitor and maintain comms with CSU + Azure. Please drop any remaining logs into the incident thread.

omar al-hassan: azure update: they are rolling a control-plane stabilization patch for PartnerX peering (ETA 2h). asked us to keep diversion for now.

sylvia chen: temporary runbook note for postmortem: checkpoints -> confirm BGP neighbor flaps, validate conntrack thresholds (increase syn backlog during maintenance windows?), add automated detection for DNS resolver flip (alerts if >5% NXDOMAIN in 5m), and add an emergency playbook to divert impacted prefixes automatically.

katie nguyen: tagging for postmortem and follow-up: product-eng, netinfra, csu. I'll create the incident ticket with initial customer impact numbers.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Severity set to SEV2 by sylvia chen at 1765432450.

sylvia chen: quick note — we saw one customer service (RIV) report token validation errors that were actually downstream timeouts; clarified with them and they removed the alert. No data loss reported.

cheng li: monitoring: adding short-term smoke tests across uaenorth -> backups: `for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://private-api.uae.redwood/test || echo fail; done` results now showing 200s ~ 96% of runs.

omar al-hassan: leaving logs/pcap link in the thread: https://s3.redwood-infra/incident/1765432109/pcap.tgz (internal).

oncall-shadow: taking over monitoring. If anything spikes above 5% error or Azure says ETA moved, I'll escalate back. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

sylvia chen: closing live incident coordination. We'll follow up with a full postmortem after Azure confirms fix and PartnerX stabilizes.

katie nguyen: filed incident ticket INC-2024-1623 and initial customer advisory draft in #customer-notices.

incident-bot: Incident thread archived to incidents channel history at 1765433200.
